121277.subject: Botany
121277.text: Which of the following best describes the metabolism of bacteria as a group?
121277.sol: Though the bacterial structure is very simple, they are very complexin behaviour. Compared to many other organisms, bacteria as a groupshow the most extensive metabolic diversity. Some of the bacteria areautotrophic, i.e., they synthesise their own food from inorganic substrates.They may be photosynthetic autotrophic or chemosynthetic autotrophic.The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs, i.e., they depend on otherorganisms or on dead organic matter for food.

121333.subject: Botany
121333.text: What happens to the parental nucleus after the dikaryotic stage?
121333.sol: When a fungus reproduces sexually, two haploid hyphae of compatible mating types come together and fuse. In some fungi the fusion of two haploid cells immediately results in diploid cells (2n). However, in other fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes), an interveningdikaryotic stage (n + n, i.e., two nuclei per cell) occurs; such a condition is called a dikaryon and the phase is called dikaryophase of fungus. 121481.subject: Botany
121481.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. The asexual spores in Ascomycetes are formed in Conidiosphores 2. Sexual spores in Ascomycetes are called Ascospores 3. Mycelium of ascomycetes is branched and aseptate 4. examples of ascomycetes albugo and ustilago.
121481.sol: mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores in Ascomycetes are conidia produced exogenously on the special mycelium called conidiophores. Conidia on germination produce mycelium. Sexual spores are called ascospores which are produced endogenously in sac like asci (singular ascus). These asci are arranged in different types of fruiting bodies called ascocarps.

121521.subject: Botany
121521.text: Virus Type Example and Feature A. Plant viruses 1. Double-stranded DNA virus B. Bacteriophages 2. Single-stranded RNA virus C. Animal viruses 3. Crystallizable with a protein coat D. Viruses causing diseases like smallpox and AIDS 4. Single or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA virus
121521.sol: A - 2: Plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA and can cause symptoms such as mosaic formation. B - 1: Bacteriophages are typically double-stranded DNA viruses that infect bacteria. C - 4: Animal viruses can have single or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA, causing various diseases in animals. D - 3: Viruses that cause diseases like smallpox and AIDS can be crystallized and have a protein coat, reflecting their structural characteristics.

121532.subject: Botany
121532.text: Organisms living in salty areas are called as
121532.sol: Organisms living in salty areas are called Halophiles.

121723.subject: Botany
121723.text: Besides starch, what do pyrenoids contain?
121723.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. 123523.subject: Botany
123523.text: What is the starting point of all living organisms?
123523.sol: Are you aware that all organisms, even the largest, start their life from a single cell ? You may wonder how a single cell then goes on to form such large organisms. Growth and reproduction are characteristics of cells, indeed of all living organisms. All cells reproduce by dividing into two, with each parental cell giving rise to two daughter cells each time they divide. These newly formed daughter cells can themselves grow and divide, giving rise to a new cell population that is formed by the growth and division

123874.subject: Botany
123874.text: During the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell doubles from its initial value, but there is no increase in the chromosome number. Which phase of the cell cycle is directly responsible for bringing about this change?
123874.sol: During the S phase (Synthesis phase) of the cell cycle, DNA replication takes place. This results in the doubling of the amount of DNA per cell (for example, from 2C to 4C). However, because the newly synthesized sister chromatids remain attached at the centromere, there is no increase in the chromosome number. A cell that had a diploid number of chromosomes (2n) at G₁ will still have 2n chromosomes at the end of the S phase. 124070.subject: Botany
options: A chromosome with a middle centromere forming two equal arms
A chromosome with a centromere slightly away from the middle
A chromosome with a centromere close to its end
A chromosome with a terminal centromere
124070.sol: Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere .

124461.subject: Botany
124461.text: Protein synthesis in an animal cell occurs

on ribosomes present in cytoplasm as well as in mitochondria
only on ribosomes attached to the nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum
on ribosomes present in the nucleolus as well as in cytoplasm
124461.sol: Protein synthesis takes place on ribosomes. In an eukaryotic cell ribosomes are present in cytoplasm, mitochondria and chloroplasts. So, in these places protein synthesis take place.

124722.subject: Botany

(II) It promotes female flowers in cucumbers, thereby increasing the yield. (III) It is chemically a derivative of terpenes. (IV) It promotes horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis

Statement (I) is correct: Ethylene enhances the respiration rate during fruit ripening, a phenomenon known as respiratory climactic. 124785.sol: According to NCERT, auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, an application widely used for plant propagation. Auxins also promote flowering in pineapples. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening, hastening the ripening of fruits like tomatoes and apples. It is also used to initiate flowering and for synchronising fruit-set in pineapples. Therefore, 'X' is auxin and 'Y' is ethylene. Answer: X - Auxin, Y - Ethylene

124907.subject: Botany
124907.text: Which organisms can prepare their own food?
124907.sol: Only green plants and cyanobacteria can prepare their own food; by the process of photosynthesis they trap light energy and convert it into chemical energy that is stored in the bonds of carbohydrates like glucose, sucrose and starch. We must remember that in green plants too, not all cells, tissues and organs photosynthesize; only cells containing chloroplasts, that are most often located in the superficial layers, carry out photosynthesis. To counteract uncertainties and loss of pollen grains
To ensure pollen sticks to the stigma

It synchronizes stigma receptivity with pollen release

126166.sol: Artificial hybridisation is one of the major approaches of crop improvement programme. 126951.sol: The chitin (= polyglycosamine) is an acetate of mucopolysaccharide called glycosamine which is formed by the combination of polysaccharide with small peptide molecules. The basic unit (monomer) of chitin is N -acetylglucosamine, monomers are joined by 1-4 linkages.

126952.subject: Botany
126952.sol: Arachidonic acid is polyunsaturated (i.e., have more than one double bond) and essential fatty acids. 127062.subject: Botany
127062.text: A lake near a village suffered heavy mortality of fishes within a few days. Consider the following reasons for this?
options: Lots of urea and phosphate fertilizer were used in the vicinity.
The area was sprayed with DDT by an aircraft.
The lake water turned green and stinky.
Phytoplankton polulations in the lake declined initially thereby greatly reducing photosynthesis.
127062.sol: Part of fertilizers added to crop fields are passed down to water bodies during rains through surface run-off. Presence of extra nutrients brings about dense growth of plant and animal life. The phenomenon is called eutrophication. Eutrophication leads to organic loading, depletion of oxygen, death of animals and fouling of water.

6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d79.subject: Biology
6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d79.text: Select the incorrect statement regarding the structure and types of nephrons in the human kidney.
options: A minute vessel of the peritubular capillary network runs parallel to the Henle's loop forming a 'U' shaped va
The Malpighian corpuscle, proximal convoluted tubule, and distal convoluted tubule are situated in the cortica
The vasa recta is well-developed and prominent in cortical nephrons.
In the majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is short and extends only very little into the medulla.
6a104ffe8b46719ce7976d79.sol: In the human kidney, nephrons are of two types: cortical nephrons and juxtamedullary nephrons. In cortical nephrons, the loop of Henle is short and extends only very little into the medulla. The vasa recta is highly reduced or absent in these nephrons. In juxtamedullary nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla. The vasa recta is well-developed and prominent in these nephrons. Therefore, the statement that the vasa recta is well-developed and prominent in cortical nephrons is incorrect

6a7a1ff8c56bac348813447e.text: Which of the following sets of transition metal ions exhibits a green colour in aqueous solution?
options: V ³⁺, Fe ³⁺, Ni ²⁺
V ²⁺, Fe ²⁺, Ni ²⁺
V ²⁺, Cr ³⁺, Mn ³⁺
V ³⁺, Fe ²⁺, Ni ²⁺
6a7a1ff8c56bac348813447e.sol: According to the characteristic colours of 3d transition metal ions in aqueous solutions: V ³⁺ is green. Fe ²⁺ is green. Ni ²⁺ is green. Other ions mentioned have different colours: Fe ³⁺ is yellow. V ²⁺ is violet. Cr ³⁺ is violet. Mn ³⁺ is violet. Thus, the set where all ions are green is V ³⁺, Fe ²⁺, Ni ²⁺ . Answer: V ³⁺, Fe ²⁺, Ni ²⁺
